android.evidence: upstream README lists Android and release 1.52.0 publishes a signed APK

desktop.evidence: upstream README lists Linux, Windows and Mac support

raspberry_pi.evidence: portable Linux/C runtime is a plausible Pi target, but this proof did not establish an explicit Raspberry Pi support statement

extended.note: macOS is documented upstream; iOS is not claimed by this proof

maintenance.note: stable release is materially older than sherpa-onnx and should be rechecked during admission

quality.naturalness: formant synthesis; intentionally less natural than neural TTS

benchmark.reason: Researcher manual proof does not execute upstream candidate code

integration_assessment.adapter_model: Library-owned voice.tts.v1 adapter over eSpeak NG shared-library synthesis API
strengths: useful deterministic fallback when neural TTS is unavailable
weaknesses: Raspberry Pi must be validated explicitly before target certification
speech naturalness is substantially below modern neural engines
stable release is older than the preferred candidate
voice.tts.v1 remains a logical boundary rather than a detailed adapter API

recommendation: Independent ultra-light voice.tts fallback candidate; retain for admission only with GPL distribution review and explicit Raspberry Pi validation.
